question.text: If an AMC wants to change the fundamental attributes of a scheme (like its investment objective), what must it offer to existing investors?

answer.text: An exit option without any exit load
Higher returns for the next year
Nothing — the AMC can change anything without informing investors

explanation.text: The Logic: When an AMC changes the fundamental attributes of a scheme (for example, the investment objective, asset allocation pattern, or scheme type), it must give existing investors the option to exit without any exit load. This protects unitholders who may not agree with the revised attributes of the scheme. The Trap: The AMC cannot make such changes silently. The workbook states that the exit window must be kept open for the time stipulated by SEBI, rather than specifying a fixed number of days in the workbook itself. Note: When such changes are announced, proactively inform clients so they can review the revised scheme attributes and decide whether to stay invested or exercise the no-load exit option within the stipulated window.
